Biggest injury concerns for Week 11

Players with early starts

ACTIVE

Darren Waller, TE, Panthers (knee): Waller is active for Week 11 after limited practices Thursday and Friday. Waller is a TD-dependent streaming option. Some preferred TE plays are Mark Andrews and Chig Okonkwo. Waller should be used over Brenton Strange, Dallas Goedert and Mike Gesicki.

Kyle Monangai, RB, Bears (toe): Monangai is off the injury report and active for Week 11. He has not played since Week 4. Still, he is in the mix as a flex option due to a matchup against the Saints. New Orleans has allowed the fourth-most rushing yards to RBs, as well as the second-most RB fantasy points.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 11 Buzz 

Week 11 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 11

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Caleb Douglas, WR, Dolphins (shoulder): Douglas had been limited at practice this week before elevating to full participation on Friday. He is off the injury report and active for Week 11. He has seen eight targets in both of his past two games and has scored double-digit fantasy points in three of his four games since returning from injury. While he is more volatile with QB Kyle McCord, Douglas is in the flex conversation, especially given all the byes.

Jordyn Tyson, WR, Saints (chest): Tyson was limited at practice this week but is active for Week 11. Consider him to be a WR2 (with a lot more upside). Tyson saw a 38% target share and 50% air yard share last week in his first NFL game with no limitations. Tyson has lined up over half the time in the slot since he returned. Bears slot CB Kyler Gordon is out, which should provide a boost for Tyson. In a game in which the Saints will have to put up points, Tyson should be started.

DeVonta Smith, WR, Eagles (hamstring): Smith has practiced in full this week and is off the Eagles' practice report. He is active for Week 11. He will be the top target for Joe Milton and the Eagles. While his production likely takes a hit without Jalen Hurts in the huddle, Milton does throw a good deep ball. That could lead to some big plays for Smith. He should be valued as a low-end WR2 in his first game back on the field. Note: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) has been placed on IR  and will not return this week for the Eagles.

Baker Mayfield, QB, Buccaneers (ankle): Mayfield is active for Week 11. While he has not been a great fantasy option himself this season, his presence has elevated Tampa Bay's playmakers, especially Emeka Egbuka. Still, Mayfield is a streaming option this week against the Lions, who allow the second-most QB fantasy PPG.

articles.headline: Milan into top four as classy Pulisic solo goal caps Serie A rout
articles.description: AC Milan racked up their biggest win of the season under Ruben Amorim as Frosinone were beaten 5-1 at San Siro on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: プリシッチの鮮やかなソロゴールで大勝、ミランがトップ4入り
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日にサン・シーロで行われたフロジノーネ戦で、ACミランは5-1で勝利し、ルベン・アモリム監督のもとで今シーズン最大の勝利を挙げた。
articles.body:
AC Milan racked up their biggest win of the season under Ruben Amorim as Frosinone were beaten 5-1 at San Siro on Sunday.

It is now five wins in six matches for Milan, who climbed into Serie A's top four and to within five points of leaders Lazio.

It was a rampaging victory earned with room to spare, and was much needed following wins for Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus.

An own goal from Gabriele Calvani and a fourth goal of the season from Gonçalo Ramos made it 2-0 early on before Patrizio Masini scored to halve the deficit for the visitors.

The second half quickly turned into a procession with goals from Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cissè making it 4-1 before Christian Pulisic got a goal to add some gloss to the scoreline.

Newly promoted Frosinone have been one of the surprise packages of the season, but dropped to seventh behind Juve after Luciano Spalletti's side extended their own unbeaten run to four games with a home win.

Calvani's own goal got Milan on their way, then Adrien Rabiot set up Ramos for a much-needed goal following a relatively slow start to life in Serie A.

The visitors hauled themselves back into contention midway through the first half through Masini, but Milan pulled clear in the second half with an excellent counter-attacking play.

Substitutes Jashari and Cisse made good on Milan's dominance before Pulisic's solo run and chipped finish completed the rout to wrap up the biggest win of Amorim's time in charge.

Information from PA was used in this recap.

articles.headline: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce's top moments at Arrowhead Stadium
articles.description: Kelce's greatest Arrowhead moments include his first catch, lots of playoff magic, and meeting the love of his life, Taylor Swift.
articles.headlineJa: カンザスシティ・チーフスのタイトエンド、トラビス・ケルシーのアローヘッド・スタジアムでの名場面
articles.descriptionJa: ケルシーのアローヘッドでの最高の瞬間には、初キャッチや数々のプレーオフでの劇的な活躍、そして最愛の人テイラー・スウィフトとの出会いなどが含まれる。
articles.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Travis Kelce gets goosebumps every time, even though the drive from his home to his place of employment, at this point in his 14-year career, is routine.

On game days, his car enters Gate 5, the road that leads to the entrance of the Kansas City Chiefs' training facility. The destination of his journey always makes Kelce smile.

"You come through the facility, and you just see Arrowhead [Stadium] pop up out of nowhere," Kelce said recently. "That's the best feeling for me."

Few players in the Chiefs' 67-year history have entered Arrowhead to put on the team's red jersey, helmet and cleats as many times as Kelce. On Sunday, against the Arizona Cardinals, Kelce became only the fourth player in franchise history -- joining Hall of Fame right guard Will Shields, kicker Nick Lowery and punter Dustin Colquitt -- to play 100 regular-season games at Arrowhead, a venue that opened in 1972. Kelce considers Arrowhead a revered place, even before the venue was the site where his relationship with Taylor Swift, his wife, became public.

Whenever Kelce's illustrious career ends -- which could happen after this season -- he will be remembered for being one of the franchise's greatest players and at minimum a three-time Super Bowl champion. He is also proud that his play, and most of his memorable highlights, will be synonymous with the history of Arrowhead, which is expected to have its final season in 2030.

"The fans love to fill that stadium and create those memories and get away from the realities of what the world is," Kelce said. "I just love the fact that they pour so much into it. It just makes you want to play that much harder for them. That definitely makes Arrowhead special."

Chiefs founder Lamar Hunt always said Arrowhead was his favorite place on earth. Kelce, 37, understands why Hunt, who died in 2006, had such a fond sentiment. Hours before kickoff, the expansive parking lots that surround the stadium host thousands of tailgating fans, many of them cooking the city's favorite cuisine: barbecue.

When driving into the stadium, Kelce often rolls down his windows to enjoy the tantalizing smell of the many cookouts, and the brief moments he can interact with fans.

"I like to just feel that feeling of being around the tailgate and the atmosphere," Kelce said. "It's just a part of the ballpark experience. I'm a fan of this game at heart, so getting that feeling of the moment building [before kickoff]. That's all a part of it for me."

Kelce's career has coincided with the Chiefs' most successful period at Arrowhead. His Chiefs teams have won 76.5% of their games in the stadium, including 16 victories in the postseason. Fans inside the venue have also been privileged to see each stage of Kelce's transformation as a player, from a talented-but-sometimes-immature phenom to a certain future Hall of Famer.

articles.headline: Poch blames 'circumstances' in painful Man United loss to Liverpool
articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino called for understanding of the "circumstances" that led to Manchester United suffering a 4-0 defeat Sunday against Liverpool in his first game as head coach.
articles.body:
LIVERPOOL, England -- Mauricio Pochettino called for understanding of the "circumstances" that led to Manchester United suffering a 4-0 defeat Sunday against Liverpool in his first game as head coach -- a loss which was the worst start for a United boss in 100 years.

United remain in the Premier League relegation zone after a humiliating result at Anfield which was sparked by Leny Yoro's eighth minute red card for a foul on Alexander Isak that referee Sam Barrott deemed to have denied a clear goalscoring opportunity.

With Yoro sent off, United were forced to face Andoni Iraola's team with 10 players for over 80 minutes and Pochettino, who stepped down from his role as coach of the United States to move to Old Trafford, said that the end result was a consequence of Yoro's dismissal.

"Today we concede four goals with 10 men and after playing 80 minutes at Anfield with 10 men," Pochettino told reporters. "I take responsibility for that, no worries, but I don't want to compare with the past. Now it is to talk about today

"But you have to look at circumstances. Otherwise to talk is so cheap. After eight minutes, 10 men, red card, concede the goal in this action and 80 minutes to play more, do you think that is easy?

"Even the best team in the world playing in these circumstances concede four goals or even more.

"We lost one game. We are not going to lose more than one the way we lost today. We feel the pain, but we keep working."

Pochettino said United should have had a penalty prior to Yoro's red card following a Jérémy Jacquet challenge on Bryan Mbeumo.

"I wasn't agreeing with the red card because I think the situation was when Isak control the ball, the ball wasn't in his control," Pochettino said. "The centre-back [Yoro] was running with him, Isak saw the control wasn't good and it is normal you delay, you stop to run, in that moment Yoro came from the back and it is like a touch like this and you go down.

"Never is a foul, but if you go two minutes before and the situation with Jacquet and Mbeumo and tell me?

"It was a penalty to Mbeumo, we can make mistake, no but we were punished and they were not."

Pochettino, meanwhile, defended his decision to start Matthijs de Ligt, despite the Netherlands defender having not started a Premier League for over a year due to a back injury. De Ligt was at fault for three goals in an error-strewn performance that questioned his selection.

"He was training," Pochettino said. "He played in the Champions League before the international duty and when we arrived, we saw the combinations.

"But I repeat again, with Jacquet it was penalty and that action after never come. One centre-back made a mistake, it was a mistake, wasn't punished and after we [De Ligt] made a mistake and was punished."

United are 19th in the Premier League and have now made their worst start to a season since 1972-73. But Pochettino insisted United have "lots of games to play" as they attempt to escape their perilous position.

articles.headline: Rio Ngumoha: Need to 'stay grounded' despite 'special' goal against Man Utd
articles.description: Rio Ngumoha has described his goal in Liverpool's 4-0 victory over Manchester United as "really special" but said he needs to "stay grounded" amid all of the external attention.
articles.body:
Rio Ngumoha has described his goal in Liverpool's 4-0 victory over Manchester United as "really special" but said he needs to "stay grounded" amid all of the external attention.

Ngumoha teed up Florian Wirtz in the first half at Anfield before finding the back of the net from a Bradley Barcola pass after the break. In doing so, he became the youngest Liverpool player to score and assist in a Premier League game since Michael Owen on Boxing Day 1997.

"Liverpool-United can't really get much bigger in my eyes," the 18 year old told BBC Match of the Day after the game. "To get the three points here at Anfield is special. It was a really important game today. These records are really special and just getting goals and helping my team is the main thing, to get three points. Hopefully I can score and assist many more.

"I just like exciting other people really, when I show everyone what I can do and get everyone off their seats. Hopefully I can keep going and keep my head on the floor and stay grounded."

Ngumoha's head coach Andoni Iraola was full of praise for the teenager in his post-match news conference and also defended referee Sam Barrott's decision to show Leny Yoro a red card for a last-man challenge on Alexander Isak in the first half.

"I think [Rio] is playing a lot of minutes on the right and on the left," Iraola said. "He is getting used to cutting inside and finishing, going outside and crossing from both sides. These are situations against 10 players where if you can give him the ball in a situation where he is one v one, he can damage any full-back."

On the red card, Iraola added: "I think it's a situation where [Yoro] is clearly the last man, it is clearly a foul. Would Alex or the 'keeper arrive first to the ball? We will never know. It's a clear foul, he's a last player, Alex goes against the 'keeper.

"It's a good moment for us because we are obviously going to spend a lot of time playing against 10 men."

articles.headline: Bulls G Norman Powell sidelined by mild hamstring injury
articles.description: Bulls guard Norman Powell has been ruled out against the Nuggets and will be reevaluated later in the week because of a mild right hamstring strain.
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- Bulls guard Norman Powell has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Nuggets because of a mild right hamstring strain.

Powell was injured during Friday night's 98-94 loss to the Washington Wizards. The Bulls said Powell will be evaluated later this week.

The 33-year-old Powell is averaging a team-high 20.8 points per game in his first season with Chicago. He scored 16 points against the Wizards on 7-for-18 shooting.

Powell signed a two-year deal with the Bulls in free agency that could be worth up to $45 million. The veteran guard played for the Miami Heat last season, averaging 21.7 points in 58 games while earning an All-Star selection for the first time.

Chicago rookie Caleb Wilson also missed the matchup with Denver. Wilson is working his way back from a broken right hand.

articles.headline: Travis Kelce passes Rob Gronkowski on TDs by TE list, alone in third all time
articles.description: Travis Kelce has passed Rob Gronkowski for third place for the most total touchdowns, including playoffs, by a tight end in league history.
articles.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, as he has done throughout this season, continued to move up in the NFL record books during Sunday's game against the Cardinals.

Kelce opened the Chiefs' scoring with an 8-yard touchdown reception from quarterback Patrick Mahomes in the first quarter. The score was significant for Kelce, who passed Rob Gronkowski for third place for the most total touchdowns, including playoffs, by a tight end in league history with 109. Only Pro Football Hall of Famers Antonio Gates (118) and Tony Gonzalez (115) have scored more.

Kelce added his 110th career touchdown on a 22-yard scoring pass from Mahomes in the second quarter.

Earlier this season, Kelce and Mahomes passed Gates and Philip Rivers for the most yards (9,365) generated by a tight end and quarterback duo in NFL history. In Week 2, Kelce broke the NFL record for the most yards after catch in NFL history, passing Hall of Fame running back Marshall Faulk.

Sunday marked Kelce's 100th regular-season game inside Arrowhead Stadium as he became just the fourth player in franchise history to accomplish such a feat since the venue opened in 1972.

In his 14th season, Kelce has once again led the Chiefs' passing attack. Entering Week 11, Kelce led the Chiefs' pass catchers with 512 receiving yards and three total touchdowns.

articles.headline: Recap: Liverpool spoil Mauricio Pochettino's debut by crushing Man United
articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino began his Man United tenure with a whimper as Liverpool ran out 4-0 winners. Relive all the action with ESPN.
articles.body:
One of the biggest matches in world soccer took center stage at Anfield on Sunday: Two of England's most storied clubs faced off as Liverpool welcomed Manchester United to Anfield in a blockbuster Premier League showdown.

The biggest storyline heading into the match was Mauricio Pochettino's Man United debut. The Argentine coach took charge of the Red Devils for the first time following the sacking of Michael Carrick and his own departure from the United States men's national team.

As a spectacle, it didn't disappoint.

Inside the first 13 minutes, United were reduced to ten men and trailed by two goals, before Liverpool eventually cruised to a commanding 4-0 victory.

Relive all the action with ESPN.

articles.headline: Mauricio Pochettino gets reality check as Liverpool ruin his Man United debut
articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino began his Manchester United career with a nightmare as his Red Devils went to Anfield and were routed 4-0 by Liverpool on Sunday.
articles.body:
LIVERPOOL, England -- Mauricio Pochettino made a nightmare start to his Manchester United career as the former United States men's national team coach saw his new side humiliated in a 4-0 defeat against Liverpool on Sunday at Anfield.

United were forced to play with ten players for more than 80 minutes after defender Leny Yoro was sent off for a foul on Alexander Isak after just eight minutes. And goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Víctor Muñoz inflicted United's heaviest defeat of the season and left the Premier League's biggest club in the relegation zone.

The win lifts Liverpool to fourth place, seven points behind leaders Arsenal, but the significance of the result is far greater for United, who have won just one game in the league all season. -- Mark Ogden

Pochettino gets reality check

Pochettino realized a dream by landing the Manchester United job, but after just eight minutes of this game, he probably wished he was still in America coaching the USMNT because Liverpool made his debut a nightmare.

Big jobs like United only tend to come up when the club is struggling, but United are really struggling, and there will be no quick fix. If Pochettino thought he could inspire an early upturn in performances, he was mistaken as United crumbled at Anfield.

But the bad news for Poch is that there are no superstars waiting in the wings to bail United out.

Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford will be fit soon, but will they make much difference? Unlikely. And Carlos Baleba will be out until the New Year with a hamstring injury, so any new-coach bounce must happen without United's best midfielder.

The players he had at Anfield are what he has to work with, and they are in the relegation zone for a reason -- they aren't good enough. Pochettino would have known that United have problems, but this will have been a reality check for the former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea coach.

United must now beat Brentford in Pochettino's first home game next Saturday to kick-start their season, but there are absolutely no guarantees that will happen. -- Ogden

Iraola gets first signature Anfield win

If Andoni Iraola is to go on and be successful at Liverpool, perhaps this will be remembered as the day his Anfield career really took flight.

The Reds' record at home in the Premier League this season has been dismal. Before Sunday, their tally of five points from five home matches was tied for the club's worst points haul to start a Premier League season (also five in 2012-13). After losing to both Arsenal and Manchester City at Anfield this term, Iraola needed a big win and, against United, he got what he had been asking for.

While the early red card for Yoro made Liverpool's assignment easier, there was much to like from the hosts as they constantly looked to charge forward and lay siege on the opposition goal.
